</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship</p><p>Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya</a> on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.</p><p>Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.       <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <description><p>Island’s labour minister, Tony Dyer, says agreement acknowledges links between Speightstown and UK city are rooted in slave trade</p><p>A town in Barbados known as “Little Bristol” has signed a “twinning’” agreement with the UK city, marking a new chapter in a centuries-long relationship rooted in the transatlantic slave trade.</p><p>Barbados says the new partnership between Speightstown and Bristol is part of its wider push for reparatory justice, built in small steps rather than around a multi-trillion-pound claim.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/23/barbados-minister-speightstown-bristol-deal-slave-trade-reparations">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba</link>
      <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Individual Australians will be able to sue big tech firms for harm suffered online under compromise deal </p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/nov/24/labor-penny-wong-us-china-anthony-albanese-final-sitting-week-ntwnfb">Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates</a></p></li><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily political email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Big tech companies may face “multibillion-dollar” fines and individuals could sue social media companies in court under <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/oct/28/emotional-intimacy-ai-chatbots-ban-digital-duty-of-care-laws-australian-politics">Australia’s new digital duty of care</a> laws, with the Greens to support the bill’s passage after extracting major amendments from Labor.</p><p>From late 2027, Australians will also be able opt out of addictive online algorithms under the new legislation, while <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/sep/09/labor-australians-opt-out-online-algorithms-how-change-feed#:~:text=A%20few%20features%20will%20be%20classified%20as%20having%20%E2%80%9Cnegative%20behavioural%20impacts%E2%80%9D%3A%20endless%20scroll">the “endless scroll” of social media feeds</a> may also cease.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/24/social-media-big-tech-fines-global-revenue-australia-digital-duty-care-laws">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Hunter Valley Operations expansion in New South Wales would allow additional 430m tonnes of coal to be extracted and burned</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2025/mar/10/sign-up-for-the-clear-air-australia-environment-newsletter-with-adam-morton?CMP=cvau_sfl">Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here</a></p></li></ul><p>Climate campaigners are urging the Albanese government to heed a “line in the sand” warning on fossil fuels issued by dozens of countries at a UN climate summit and refuse a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/sep/30/hunter-valley-coal-project-singleton-ipc-planning-decision">massive coalmine expansion</a> planned in New South Wales.</p><p>A proposed agreement at the Cop31 negotiations in Turkey failed after a list of nations – including European Union members, Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, Norway and Belize – said they would not support it unless it included an explicit statement that the world needed to transition away from fossil fuels.</p><p><strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2025/mar/10/sign-up-for-the-clear-air-australia-environment-newsletter-with-adam-morton?CMP=copyembed">Sign up to get climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter</a></strong></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/24/campaigners-urge-albanese-government-to-reject-climate-bomb-coalmine-expansion-after-cop31">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘State-sanctioned theft’: Australian news outlets demand content is protected from AI scraping – as it happened</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/nov/24/labor-penny-wong-us-china-anthony-albanese-final-sitting-week-ntwnfb</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>The government will save more than it spends, says <strong>Jim Chalmers</strong>, but it won’t be a “slash and burn” budget update.</p><p>Unlike the federal budget, where we get plenty of notice of when it will be handed down, the government only gives us a few days notice for the mid-financial year economic and fiscal outlook (or Myefo).</p><p>There’s still a fair bit of work to do to finalise it all, but we’ve made enough progress to be confident that at this stage there will be a modest net save in the budget.</p><p>We’re not going to slash and burn in the budget where that would impact the payments that people receive or where it would impact some of the more sensitive parts of the economy. But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times.</p><p>You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/24/ebikes-screens-and-failing-manners-pose-challenge-for-dutch-cycling-culture</link>
      <description><p>Awareness campaign reminds public ‘traffic is a team sport’ amid less civility and more collisions on roads</p><p>For decades the Netherlands has been famed for its proud cycling culture, with a network of 23,000 miles of bike paths used by everyone from children under eight to adults over 80.</p><p>In recent years, however, like so many countries around the world, it has seen a dramatic change in the type of vehicles using those lanes: no longer the preserve of pedal bikes, they are used by all manner of two-wheeled vehicles including electric cargo bikes, thick-tyred “fatbikes”, speed pedelecs, electric scooters and even some micro cars.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/24/ebikes-screens-and-failing-manners-pose-challenge-for-dutch-cycling-culture">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Burnham says it would be ‘unthinkable’ to rejoin EU without referendum</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-deal-eu</link>
      <description><p>Prime minister also says former Tory premiers who have criticised revival of Brexit debate are ‘stuck in the past’</p><p>Andy Burnham has said it would be “unthinkable” for the UK to rejoin the EU without holding another referendum, offering his strongest commitment yet to directly consulting the public if he concludes Britain should go back in.</p><p>The prime minister is planning to set out the long-term options for closer ties with the bloc next month, with concrete steps coming after the next general election, as he has pledged to stick to Labour’s manifesto red lines.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-deal-eu">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenes</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-chief-executive</link>
      <description><p>Share price surges as chipmaker reverses decision to remove chief executive after US president ‘convinced’ its board</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nils-pratley-on-finance/2026/nov/23/nvidia-board-jensen-huang-return">Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/jensen-huang-affair-timeline">Timeline: fall and comeback of Jensen Huang</a></p></li></ul><p>Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after Donald Trump directly intervened with the US AI chipmaker’s board of directors, in a stunning reversal of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">the tech billionaire’s downfall</a>.</p><p>Speaking on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s surprise announcement that Huang had been restored to the top job – less than two weeks after he resigned – Trump said he had “convinced” the board to do it. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC. Huang had resigned after reports of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-chief-executive">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/jensen-huang-nvidia-john-kennedy</link>
      <description><p>John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips</p><p>Invoking Greek mythology, the US senator John Kennedy has characterized former <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nvidia">Nvidia</a> chief executive officer <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/jensen-huang">Jensen Huang</a>’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the <a href="https://x.com/atrupar/status/2124514031209980207?a=ArDF3m1PBQGZjNDPrME&amp;s=20">most expensive</a> sex since Helen of Troy”.</p><p>The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/jensen-huang-testify-congress-nvidia-affair-spy">put at risk</a> by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/jensen-huang-nvidia-john-kennedy">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/jensen-huang">Jensen Huang</category>

      <description><p>Amid air chaos, travelers will have to navigate an outdated system (and complex company policies if it all goes wrong)</p><p>Millions of people are planning to fly in the US over the Thanksgiving holiday, just two weeks after the US Federal Aviation Administration’s 13 November <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/faa-ground-stop-flights-explained">ground stop</a> halted all flights nationwide for the first time since 9/11 (aside from a brief halt in 2023).</p><p>In the chaos that ensued, some travelers embarked on <a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/royalcaribbean/comments/1xvkopq/comment/19smxjywidlcw/?context=3">overnight drives</a> to catch cruise ships and <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/women-stranded-faa-ground-stop-buy-ford-bronco-27-hour-road-trip-rcna609629">bought new cars</a> to make business meetings. Many had to simply cancel their plans and incur the costs that came with it. More than 18,000 flights were cancelled at a potential cost to travelers of $1.9bn in lost time and related expenses, <a href="https://www.andersoneconomicgroup.com/analysis-nationwide-ground-stop-cost-travelers-nearly-2-billion/">Anderson Economic Group estimates</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/23/thanksgiving-air-travel-us-explainer">Continue reading...</a></description>

French President Emmanuel Macron has announced €350 million in funding for civil aviation research, and plans to create new industrial zones with simplified administrative procedures, as France looks to accelerate its reindustrialisation. The announcement came during the second Choose France business summit focused on the home market.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a2ef3750-e74c-11f1-a595-b587b1fd65db</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:46:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg">© Manon Cruz/Pool via Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Major cyberattack hits IT systems at Guadeloupe university hospital</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261123-major-cyberattack-hits-it-systems-at-guadeloupe-university-hospital</link><description>
A major cyberattack has disrupted the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe, affecting its operations and forcing it to activate its emergency response plan and postponing non-emergency procedures.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dee6caee-e728-11f1-80df-9f0d9c8f7db3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:45:02 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg">© Carla Bernhardt/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ad79414-e5c2-11f1-8bc6-7d93519529c2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:43:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-french-court-finds-racism-played-role-in-police-beating-of-black-music-producer</link><description>
A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eadc87ac-e58a-11f1-b7fe-efd3e07e368d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:41:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-national-assembly-backs-greater-legal-protection-for-police-using-firearms</link><description>
France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/brentford-everton-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. David Moyes made history for Everton, edging clear of Harry Catterick by overseeing his 593rd game in charge of the club, but calamitous defending ruined the Scot’s evening and defeat to Brentford was inevitable after James Tarkowski received his first red card in 351 Premier League appearances.</p><p>Those in Tarkowski’s corner will claim the Everton captain’s tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk would not have been a foul back in the day. This, though, was not a “game’s gone” moment. Not that sort of player? The reality is Tarkowski’s back catalogue features plenty of orange card tackles, meaning there was always likely to come a time when his luck ran out.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/brentford-everton-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/kevin-de-bruyne-napoli-manchester-city-champions-league</link>
      <description><p>Even without the charges, the Belgian maestro will be an unwelcome throwback to happier times for Enzo Maresca</p><p>As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times. Kevin De Bruyne will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday, evoking the greatest period of Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge when they won four straight Premier League titles and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jun/10/rodri-breaks-internazionale-resistance-to-seal-manchester-citys-treble-glory">the Champions&nbsp;League</a>.</p><p>In Europe, things are comfortable for Enzo Maresca, with three wins from four, but they have collected a solitary point from 12 domestically recently. They are struggling to score and conceding too easily at the back, leading the Italian to experiment in his attempts to find solutions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/kevin-de-bruyne-napoli-manchester-city-champions-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Nwaneri at risk of becoming Arsenal’s forgotten teenager on return with Dortmund</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/ethan-nwaneri-arsenal-dortmund-mikel-arteta-champions-league</link>
      <description><p>Youngest player to appear in Premier League is struggling to establish himself on loan at the Bundesliga club</p><p>Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/sep/18/arsenals-ethan-nwaneri-becomes-youngest-premier-league-player-at-15">youngest player to appear in the Premier League</a>, with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/30/max-dowman-journey-billericay-to-history-with-arsenal">highly anticipated debut</a>. But after a week when Arsenal published <a href="https://www.arsenal.com/news/max-dowmans-incredible-list-of-records-for-club-and-country-azbFG5M3BWVo">an article</a> dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager.</p><p>Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday, although the 19-year-old will probably be on the bench, having not started for the German club yet in the competition. Despite making a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut, against Hoffenheim, he has not started in the league since 17 October and has yet to complete more than 65 minutes in a Bundesliga match.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/ethan-nwaneri-arsenal-dortmund-mikel-arteta-champions-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Emery insists no change of plan for Aston Villa despite Galatasaray surface</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/unai-emery-no-change-of-plan-aston-villa-galatasaray-surface</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>‘Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible,’ says Villa manager</p></li><li><p>Turkish champions had to move game on Saturday</p></li></ul><p>Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions League game at ­Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”.</p><p>Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work. Galatasaray played Saturday’s victory over Samsunspor at Basaksehir Fatih Terim stadium, a significantly smaller ground named after the former Turkey manager, who played for and managed Galatasaray.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/unai-emery-no-change-of-plan-aston-villa-galatasaray-surface">Continue reading...</a></description>

up for our free newsletter here</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/19/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">United’s victory at Anfield last season</a> was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.</p><p>Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">lost only 4-0</a>. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/mar/05/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023</a>. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/mauricio-pochettino-can-now-see-just-how-desperate-manchester-united-are">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds</p><p>It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat.</p><p>The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass.       <title>WSL talking points: captain Spence inspires Spurs’ shock win at City and Lionesses impress</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/wsl-talking-points-tottenham-london-city-lionesses-chelsea-arsenal</link>
      <description><p>We may have a proper title race on our hands as City and Chelsea drop points and LCL strengthen their grip on third place</p><p>Drew Spence rolled back the years with a vintage performance as her Tottenham side produced a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">shock 3-1 victory</a> away against the defending champions, Manchester City. The 34-year-old marshalled the midfield and then had the vision to thread an outstanding through ball that split the City defence and found the run of Matilda Vinberg, who put Spurs 2-1 up. “She’s unbelievable. There are so many more gears in Drew and I wish I’d been able to work with her a bit earlier [in my career] because her leadership is second to none,” the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said of the club captain. “Her performance levels, since I’ve been here, week on week have grown. She is covering every blade of grass and leads by example. For me, she’s one of the best midfielders in the league.” <strong>Tom Garry</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">Match report: Manchester City 1-3 Tottenham</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/wsl-talking-points-tottenham-london-city-lionesses-chelsea-arsenal">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/nwsl-championship-washington-spirit-kansas-city-current</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Current’s opener came direct from a corner kick</p></li><li><p>Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time</p></li><li><p>Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final</p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/21/washington-spirit-kansas-city-current-nwsl-championship-live-updates">Read Jeff Rueter’s minute-by-minute report</a></p></li></ul><p>It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.</p><p>Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute <em>Olimpico</em> from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/nwsl-championship-washington-spirit-kansas-city-current">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/manchester-city-fulham-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four, but at least against Fulham they ended a three-game losing run. As they await their fate after being found guilty of financial breaches, their form has slumped. This passive draw was met with boos from the home fans.</p><p>Arguments will be made over Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal but City did not deserve anything more. The Norwegian uncharacteristically missed a number of fine chances as Rodrigo Muniz took advantage of City’s porous defence. They had to rely on Elliot Anderson to get anything out of the fixture.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/manchester-city-fulham-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United.       <title>Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/sevilla-real-betis-seville-derby-la-liga-kike-salas</link>
      <description><p>Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change</p><p>“If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, <em>this</em> was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ikiN2ah9DL4">Pelé against the Nazis</a>. Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears.</p><p>In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of <a href="https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37625798/sevilla-real-betis-laliga-best-rivalry-city-lives-sport">a city divided</a>, Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled <em>the </em>game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/sevilla-real-betis-seville-derby-la-liga-kike-salas">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c7f51d20-e757-11f1-8c0c-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/Couv-Afrique-FIFA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c7f51d20-e757-11f1-8c0c-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/Couv-Afrique-FIFA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">10565f16-e758-11f1-bac8-75c9eaf1ef66</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:19:59 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Élément Terre, la quotidienne</category><title>Après l'échec de la COP31, quel avenir pour la diplomatie climatique ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/%C3%A9l%C3%A9ment-terre-la-quotidienne/20261123-apr%C3%A8s-l-%C3%A9chec-de-la-cop31-quel-avenir-pour-la-diplomatie-climatique</link><description>
La COP31 s'est achevée sans accord final. Les pays producteurs de pétrole ont fait pression pour que la sortie des énergies fossiles ne soit pas mentionnée dans la déclaration. Plus d'une centaine de pays se sont en conséquence opposé à son adoption sans cette mention. Cette COP était la première depuis l'annonce par l'ONU du dépassement "inévitable" d'1,5°C de réchauffement climatique. "Le monde ne peut pas se permettre que cela se reproduise", a jugé le chef de l'ONU Climat, Simon Stiell. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db1ec12e-e75e-11f1-aaee-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-371671ce.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db1ec12e-e75e-11f1-aaee-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-371671ce.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4ad0eb0e-e760-11f1-b781-ad27a2c984c6</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:06:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Audrey RACINE</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Belgique : le pays en grève  contre l’austérité  du gouvernement</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-belgique-le-pays-en-gr%C3%A8ve-contre-l-aust%C3%A9rit%C3%A9-du-gouvernement</link><description>
Alors que des dizaines de milliers de Belges protestaient contre l'austérité ce lundi 23 novembre, le roi Philippe a accordé un délai supplémentaire à Bart De Wever pour tenter de débloquer les négociations budgétaires. Le Premier ministre s'est donné jusqu'à la fin de l'année pour trouver un accord au sein de sa coalition, faute de quoi ce sera la fin de son gouvernement.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fcb36440-e75c-11f1-93ff-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/miniabelgique.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fcb36440-e75c-11f1-93ff-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/miniabelgique.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1a33ac50-e75d-11f1-8c11-4579bb4eb38e</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:03:23 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Trois ans après l'homicide de Nahel Merzouk, 17 ans, tué à bout portant par un tir de policier à la suite d'un refus d'obtempérer, la cour d'appel de Versailles a ordonné un procès pour meurtre à l'encontre du policier responsable de la mort du jeune homme dans cette affaire qui avait provoqué des nuits d'émeutes en France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/401d335e-e7e0-11f1-b649-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D84V2NQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/401d335e-e7e0-11f1-b649-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D84V2NQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c802ce5a-e7e0-11f1-9eaf-03e929159d16</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:27:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/401d335e-e7e0-11f1-b649-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D84V2NQ.jpg">© Zakaria Abdelkalfi, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Ouverture du Congrès des maires sur fond de bataille pour l'Élysée</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261124-ouverture-du-congr%C3%A8s-des-maires-sur-fond-de-bataille-pour-l-%C3%A9lys%C3%A9e</link><description>
La puissante Association des maires de France (AMF) se réunit du 24 au 26 novembre à Paris, où les candidats à l'élection présidentielle vont se presser, en particulier ceux en quête des 500 parrainages nécessaires à leur candidature. Mais ce rendez-vous annuel sera surtout marqué par l'élection de son président. Déjà candidat à la présidentielle, David Lisnard espère également renouveler son mandat à la tête de l'AMF.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">844245cc-e52b-11f1-ab61-a5c9daa303ca</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 21:54:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg">© Benoit PEYRUCQ / AFP/Archives</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Johann Chapoutot : "La dédiabolisation du RN est véritablement un mythe"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261120-johann-chapoutot-la-d%C3%A9diabolisation-du-rn-est-v%C3%A9ritablement-un-mythe</link><description>

Comment comprendre cette progression ? Quelle est la responsabilité de la classe politique dans cette évolution ? Quelles conséquences sur notre démocratie ? Johann Chapoutot, professeur d'histoire contemporaine, auteur de "La bascule, Allemagne 1933" (éditions Gallimard), était l'Invité d'Au cœur de l'info. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20054536-e522-11f1-9d9f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-200854-202823-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20054536-e522-11f1-9d9f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-200854-202823-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">141cd51a-e525-11f1-8891-754dc11be848</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 20:58:03 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Police : la loi sur la présomption de légitime défense définitivement adoptée par le Parlement</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-police-la-loi-sur-la-pr%C3%A9somption-de-l%C3%A9gitime-d%C3%A9fense-d%C3%A9finitivement-adopt%C3%A9e-par-le-parlement</link><description>
Vivement combattue dans la rue par ses opposants qui l'assimilent à un "permis de tuer", l'instauration d'une présomption d'usage légal des armes par les forces de l'ordre a été définitivement adoptée au Parlement vendredi soir, à la veille d'une nouvelle journée de mobilisation sociale.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec88460c-e514-11f1-8bce-43bc8e8d3f8d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 19:02:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg">© Geoffroy van der Hasselt, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fuites au ministère de l'Intérieur : comment le RN a progressivement séduit les hauts fonctionnaires</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-fuites-au-minist%C3%A8re-de-l-int%C3%A9rieur-comment-le-rn-a-progressivement-s%C3%A9duit-les-hauts-fonctionnaires</link><description>
Le parquet de Paris soupçonne l'ancien secrétaire général de Beauvau et actuel préfet du Loiret et de la région Centre-Val de Loire, Hugues Moutouh, d'avoir informé le Rassemblement national sur des enquêtes judiciaires visant le parti. Une affaire qui illustre l'influence grandissante du parti lepéniste dans les hautes sphères de l'État.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">845e625a-e4fb-11f1-8ece-9d792c6a9305</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:12:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg">© Pascal Guyot, AFP</source><dc:creator>Louis CHAHUNEAU</dc:creator></item><item><category>Outre-Mer</category><title>De l'océan Indien aux Caraïbes, la sécheresse frappe plusieurs territoires d'Outre-mer</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/outre-mer/20261120-de-l-oc%C3%A9an-indien-aux-cara%C3%AFbes-la-s%C3%A9cheresse-frappe-plusieurs-territoires-d-outre-mer</link><description>
La sécheresse s'installe durablement en Outre-mer. Le manque d'eau fragilise les cultures et menace les récoltes aux Antilles et à La Réunion. La situation est également très préoccupante en Guyane, où le niveau du fleuve continue de baisser.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d5ba9aa2-e4f5-11f1-a177-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e00d5d0f.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d5ba9aa2-e4f5-11f1-a177-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e00d5d0f.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">668bbe98-e4ca-11f1-b006-117a06c45e07</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:36:16 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator></dc:creator></item><item><category>ActuElles</category><title>Les féminicides, la partie émergée du contrôle coercitif</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/actuelles/20261120-les-f%C3%A9minicides-la-partie-%C3%A9merg%C3%A9e-du-contr%C3%B4le-coercitif</link><description>
Les féminicides font aussi des victimes invisibles : les proches des femmes assassinées, confrontées à un deuil impossible et à des embûches judiciaires. Dans 75 % des cas, le féminicide survient sans violences physiques préalables, mais au terme d'une période de contrôle coercitif :  une prison invisible faite d'emprise et de violences psychologiques, explique l'historienne Christelle Taraud, qui décrit des victimes "zombifiées" par leur tortionnaire.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/804fd37e-e4e7-11f1-94db-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/actuelles-4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/804fd37e-e4e7-11f1-94db-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/actuelles-4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">012b0ea0-e4e8-11f1-954f-b12e286687bf</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:46:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Laure MANENT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Gérard Depardieu et Michel Houellebecq accusés de viol en réunion et d'agressions sexuelles</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-g%C3%A9rard-depardieu-et-michel-houellebecq-accus%C3%A9s-de-viol-en-r%C3%A9union-et-d-agressions-sexuelles</link><description>
Gérard Depardieu est de nouveau accusé de viol – en réunion cette fois, avec la complicité supposée de l'écrivain Michel Houellebecq, selon des sources proches du dossier, confirmant vendredi des révélations de Mediapart. Les faits, dénoncés par une comédienne, remonteraient au tournage du film "Thalasso" en 2018.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/112bfeb0-e4f0-11f1-97c4-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/5b316d0d8e9e019339c005a7e2173a2aacfd39e4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/112bfeb0-e4f0-11f1-97c4-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/5b316d0d8e9e019339c005a7e2173a2aacfd39e4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">11ebaaf8-e4f0-11f1-af7a-57d065e8beab</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:38:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/112bfeb0-e4f0-11f1-97c4-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/5b316d0d8e9e019339c005a7e2173a2aacfd39e4.jpg">© Dimitar Dilkoff, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Dominique de Villepin annonce sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261120-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-2027-l-ancien-premier-ministre-dominique-de-villepin-annonce-sa-candidature</link><description>
Dominique de Villepin a officialisé vendredi 20 novembre sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027. L'ex-Premier ministre se présente comme une alternative au macronisme, à La France insoumise et au Rassemblement national.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9fb85a8a-e4d6-11f1-8eb3-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/miniadefvillepin.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9fb85a8a-e4d6-11f1-8eb3-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/miniadefvillepin.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c6c746ae-e4d6-11f1-8ffb-375f4fe00708</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:42:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>La députée RN Laure Lavalette se défend d'être antisémite, se dédouane d'écrits vieux de "30 ans"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-accusations-antis%C3%A9mitisme-d%C3%A9put%C3%A9e-rn-laure-lavalette-invoque-faits-vieux-de-30-ans</link><description>
Selon une enquête publiée mercredi par le média Les Jours, la députée du Rassemblement national du Var Laure Lavalette aurait présidé, lors de ses années d'études, un syndicat étudiant dont la revue publiait des écrits antisémites. L'élue a balayé les accusations dans une interview sur BFMTV, arguant de faits vieux de "30 ans".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1684c9f4-e4bf-11f1-943c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A49893B.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1684c9f4-e4bf-11f1-943c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A49893B.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">00ba44a8-e4c1-11f1-9390-bd7bd8f937b3</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:26:06 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1684c9f4-e4bf-11f1-943c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A49893B.jpg">© Miguel Medina, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Dominique de Villepin candidat : un homme de droite populaire à gauche mais en quête d'électeurs</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-france-presidentielle-2027-dominique-de-villepin-homme-droite-populaire-gauche-sans-electeurs</link><description>
L'ancien Premier ministre Dominique de Villepin a officialisé vendredi sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027. L'homme du "non" de la France à la guerre en Irak en 2003 est revenu sur le devant de la scène ces dernières années pour ses prises de position sur les sujets internationaux, en particulier sur la guerre à Gaza. Mais sa popularité est surtout marquée à gauche, au sein d'un électorat qui ne devrait pas voter pour lui.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fd73fc2c-e433-11f1-b4e5-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/main-Villepin.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fd73fc2c-e433-11f1-b4e5-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/main-Villepin.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c0ca20de-e434-11f1-a9ea-f369f859b733</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fd73fc2c-e433-11f1-b4e5-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/main-Villepin.png">© AFP / Studio graphique, FMM</source><dc:creator>Romain BRUNET</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Yannick Jadot claque la porte des Écologistes suite au rapprochement entre Marine Tondelier et LFI</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261119-france-presidentielle-yannick-jadot-quitte-les-ecologistes-marine-tondelier-jean-luc-melenchon-glucksmann</link><description>
Les fractures deviennent apparentes chez les Écologistes, au lendemain de la main tendue de Marine Tondelier à Jean-Luc Mélenchon : Yannick Jadot, sénateur et ex-candidat écologiste à la présidentielle, a annoncé qu'il quittait le parti, tout comme le député Jérémie Iordanoff. Tous les deux préfèrent soutenir Raphaël Glucksmann.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2434c0c2-b5b2-11ec-ac2b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/France-Elysee2022-YannickJadot.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2434c0c2-b5b2-11ec-ac2b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/France-Elysee2022-YannickJadot.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">819cc766-e46d-11f1-9bfb-ffca175961e0</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 23:04:16 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2434c0c2-b5b2-11ec-ac2b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/France-Elysee2022-YannickJadot.jpg">© Damien Meyer, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>L'actualité économique et politique en Europe - RFI</title><description>Suivez l'actualité en direct dédiée au continent Européen - Les derniers reportages, news et informations en continu en Europe, Emissions, Podcast, dossiers sur RFI.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:59:55 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine: l'Union européenne propose d'interdire de compétition les athlètes russes sur son territoire</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261124-l-union-europ%C3%A9enne-propose-d-interdire-de-comp%C3%A9tition-les-athl%C3%A8tes-russes-sur-son-territoire</link><description>
Alors que les vingt-et-un « trains de sanctions » édictés par l'Union européenne contre la Russie depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en Ukraine en février 2022 ont touché les hydrocarbures, le secteur financier ou les armements, Bruxelles vient de franchir un nouveau cap dans sa volonté de faire plier le Kremlin en s'en prenant au sport et à la culture, deux valeurs centrales de la société civile. Des propositions qui pourraient toutefois avoir du mal à se concrétiser du fait qu'elles puissent être considérées comme une attaque directe contre les citoyens russes...
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4a1460cc-e7cb-11f1-87d4-9fbe8f526646</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 06:29:46 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg">© Reuters/Yves Herman </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Accents d'Europe</category><title>Dix ans après le référendum sur le Brexit... le Bregret?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/accents-d-europe/20261123-dix-ans-apr%C3%A8s-le-r%C3%A9f%C3%A9rendum-sur-le-brexit-le-bregret</link><description>
Dix ans après le référendum sur le Brexit qui a présidé au départ effectif du Royaume-Uni de l’Europe... Londres opère lentement, mais sûrement un rapprochement avec le continent. Le Brexit a causé plus de mal que de bien, a résumé le nouveau Premier ministre travailliste Andy Burnham, qui n’exclut pas un retour de son pays dans l’UE. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bfc34f0-e45c-11f1-8d7f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322414753525.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bfc34f0-e45c-11f1-8d7f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322414753525.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">96183ba6-e762-11f1-a96c-7b5726cadb9b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 20:05:25 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Frédérique Lebel</dc:creator></item><item><category>La fabrique du monde</category><title>Pedro Sanchez peut-il réussir sa «remontada» et rester au pouvoir?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/la-fabrique-du-monde/20261123-pedro-sanchez-peut-il-r%C3%A9ussir-sa-remontada-et-rester-au-pouvoir</link><description>
Dernière ligne droite avant les élections législatives anticipées qui auront lieu ce dimanche 29 novembre en Espagne. Le scrutin s’annonce périlleux pour Pedro Sanchez, donné perdant dans les sondages. Spécialiste des « remontadas » spectaculaires, le chef du gouvernement socialiste pourra-t-il néanmoins faire mentir les sondages et rester aux affaires ?  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2e20faec-c08e-11f1-8911-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9RY9EA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2e20faec-c08e-11f1-8911-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9RY9EA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">14896756-e724-11f1-90c6-8324eea7e277</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:20:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Daniel Vallot</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Belgique: journée de grève nationale contre la vie chère, le trafic aérien entièrement paralysé</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261123-belgique-journ%C3%A9e-de-gr%C3%A8ve-nationale-contre-la-vie-ch%C3%A8re-le-trafic-a%C3%A9rien-enti%C3%A8rement-paralys%C3%A9</link><description>
Il n'y aura pas d'avion dans le ciel belge ce lundi 23 novembre : c'est la conséquence d'une grève nationale contre la vie chère. Alors que le gouvernement fédéral belge cherche difficilement à négocier un budget de rigueur qui vise à économiser 10 milliards d'euros au cours des prochaines années, les syndicats ont appelé à faire front commun et à une « grande mobilisation citoyenne » pour dénoncer la politique d’austérité ainsi que la baisse du pouvoir d’achat. Une journée à laquelle ont décidé de se joindre les contrôleurs aériens, ce qui va entièrement paralyser le trafic des avions toute la journée. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2b34cece-e719-11f1-9a3f-47fc1c531e42</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:00:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg">© Mark Carlson / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Hongrie: la détention provisoire d'un ancien ministre d'Orban dans une enquête de corruption prolongée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261123-hongrie-la-d%C3%A9tention-provisoire-d-un-ancien-ministre-d-orban-dans-une-enqu%C3%AAte-de-corruption-prolong%C3%A9e</link><description>
En Hongrie, Miklos Sesztak, l’ancien ministre du Développement national entre 2014 et 2018, et actuel député au Parlement hongrois, a été arrêté fin septembre. Il est soupçonné d’avoir détourné de l’argent public et d’avoir touché d’énormes pots-de-vin. Lors d’une perquisition à son domicile, la police a trouvé plusieurs coffres-forts vides. Il y a huit jours, les autorités hongroises découvraient un immense butin : près de 16 millions d’euros en liquide, cachés dans des forêts, des granges et des entrepôts. La détention provisoire de Miklos Sesztak a été prolongée jusqu’à fin janvier. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/023295d4-23b4-11f1-9c2f-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-03-19T090058Z-1009523912-RC2K7KA3JXOS-RTRMADP-3-IRAN-CRISIS-EU-SUMMIT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/023295d4-23b4-11f1-9c2f-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-03-19T090058Z-1009523912-RC2K7KA3JXOS-RTRMADP-3-IRAN-CRISIS-EU-SUMMIT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c47e8f4c-e715-11f1-a7a3-277926f246bd</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:23:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/023295d4-23b4-11f1-9c2f-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-03-19T090058Z-1009523912-RC2K7KA3JXOS-RTRMADP-3-IRAN-CRISIS-EU-SUMMIT.jpg">REUTERS - Yves Herman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Le grand invité international</category><title>Sylvie Bermann: «Les Européens sont impuissants face aux actes hostiles russes»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/le-grand-invit%C3%A9-international/20261123-sylvie-bermann-les-europ%C3%A9ens-sont-impuissants-face-aux-actes-hostiles-russes</link><description>
Sylvie Bermann, ancienne ambassadrice de France en Chine et en Russie et autrice de L'ours et le dragon. Russie-Chine : Histoire d'une amitié sans limites ? (Tallandier) est la grande invitée internationale de RFI ce 23 novembre 2026. Elle constate la poursuite de l'escalade militaire en Ukraine et des actes hostiles russes en Europe. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42a8de24-e4f3-11f1-83ae-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Hubert-V%C3%A9drine.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42a8de24-e4f3-11f1-83ae-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Hubert-V%C3%A9drine.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">26d10eb2-e500-11f1-a146-81b42dba9f2f</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 20:04:59 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Caroline de Camaret (France 24)</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Russie: six personnes placées en détention provisoire dans une affaire de «veuves noires»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-russie-six-personnes-plac%C3%A9es-en-d%C3%A9tention-provisoire-dans-une-affaire-de-veuves-noires</link><description>
C'est une affaire de « veuves noires » qui choque la Russie : dans la région de Volgograd, neuf personnes sont accusées d'avoir organisé un réseau pour récupérer les primes de militaires blessés ou tués en Ukraine, grâce à des mariages fictifs conclus avant l'engagement des soldats dans l'armée. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1853515c-e50e-11f1-8321-3bce4db5bc5f</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:25:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg">© Massimiliano Donati / Getty Images</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Le Danemark accuse la Russie d'avoir tenté d'assassiner un rappeur ukrainien</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-le-danemark-va-expulser-un-diplomate-russe-apr%C3%A8s-la-tentative-d-assassinat-d-un-ukrainien-sur-son-sol</link><description>
Le Danemark va expulser l'attaché de défense de l'ambassade de Russie après la tentative d'assassinat d'un rappeur ukrainien sur son sol, qu'il soupçonne Moscou d'avoir orchestré, a indiqué vendredi 20 novembre le ministre danois des Affaires étrangères. La diplomatie russe a promis de riposter. « Moscou donnera une réponse appropriée », a indiqué la porte-parole du ministère russe des Affaires étrangères, Maria Zakharova, citée par l'agence de presse TASS.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7863937e-e507-11f1-99b0-bbfd8e7adaf9</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:35:50 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg">AFP - EMIL HELMS</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Manifestations en Europe: «Une volonté de converger au niveau transnational et avec d'autres générations»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261120-manifestations-en-europe-une-volont%C3%A9-de-converger-au-niveau-transnational-et-avec-d-autres-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rations</link><description>
La mobilisation contre la vie chère traverse toute l'Europe : des millions de personnes sont attendues dans les rues contre la vie chère et pour le droit au logement. Ce mouvement de fond, lancé à partir de ce vendredi 20 novembre, traduit des réalités communes. Ces luttes peuvent-elles vraiment converger ? Quels modes d'action pour quelles revendications ? L’analyse du sociologue Paolo Stuppia, enseignant à Sciences Po Paris et co-auteur de Géopolitique de la jeunesse – Engagement et (dé)mobilisations, publiée aux éditions Cavalier bleu.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a69a8ac8-e4f2-11f1-a69d-dfb7bbed3c72</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:07:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>À la Une: Aleksandar Čupić, le sage à la tête du Parlement serbe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-%C3%A0-la-une-aleksandar-%C4%8Dupi%C4%87-le-sage-%C3%A0-la-t%C3%AAte-du-parlement-serbe</link><description>
Une revue de presse des Balkans en partenariat avec Le Courrier des Balkans.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eb8a088e-e4f2-11f1-8ab1-dffd4ffb6f91</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:41:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg">© Djordje Kojadinovic / Reuters</source><dc:creator>Courrier des Balkans</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>UE/Royaume-Uni: Andy Burnham annonce une «réflexion» en 2027 sur les relations à long terme</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-ue-royaume-uni-andy-burnham-annonce-une-r%C3%A9flexion-en-2027-sur-les-relations-%C3%A0-long-terme</link><description>
Pour son premier sommet avec l’UE, le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham peut s’estimer satisfait. Européens et Britanniques se sont mis d’accord sur trois dossiers concernant les jeunes, les émissions de CO2 et les normes alimentaires. La « remise à zéro » imaginée par son prédécesseur Keir Starmer pour les relations entre Londres et Bruxelles est désormais sur des rails, même si union douanière, libre-circulation et marché unique restent des lignes rouges pour les Britanniques. Les Européens affirment avoir tourné la page du Brexit et se satisfont ouvertement des accords ponctuels comme ceux qui ont été trouvés ce vendredi 20 novembre.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f35856f6-e4f2-11f1-85c2-81e9611d4583</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:30:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg">AP Photo/Marius Burgelman - Marius Burgelman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Deux missiles russes tombent en Pologne, Varsovie dénonce «une provocation»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-deux-missiles-russes-tombent-en-pologne-varsovie-d%C3%A9nonce-une-provocation</link><description>
Des missiles russes sont tombés ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 en Pologne, non loin de la frontière ukrainienne, suscitant de vives réactions de Varsovie, de l'Otan, de l'Union européenne et du Royaume-Uni, tous alliés de Kiev. Le secrétaire général de l'Otan, Mark Rutte, se rendra à Varsovie samedi.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b07d5818-e4f2-11f1-be00-dfb7bbed3c72</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:44 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg">© Kacper Pempel / Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>
